why: After any sequence of end-picks the remaining cards are a contiguous range [i..j], so the game is an interval DP: dp[i][j] = best (my score - opponent score) for the player to move on that range. Alice's score is (total + dp[0][n-1]) / 2.
hints: Whatever happens, the cards left on the table always form a contiguous block. That block is the whole game state.
Store the score difference, not two scores: dp[i][j] = max(cards[i] - dp[i+1][j], cards[j] - dp[i][j-1]), because after your pick the opponent plays optimally on the smaller range.
Fill by increasing length; Alice = (sum + dp[0][n-1]) / 2. O(n^2) time, O(n) space possible with a 1-D array.
pitfalls: Greedily taking the larger end is wrong: [1,5,233,7] needs Alice to take 7 first to secure 233.
Handle an empty array (score 0) and a single card.
Negative card values (not excluded by the source) still work with the difference DP, but not with 'always take the max end'.
constraints:
• 0 <= cards.length <= 1000 (not stated in the source; an O(n^2) DP is expected)
  • |cards[i]| <= 10^6 (not stated in the source)
